ctx.x: That's right, that's right. Then Chick made a record with him on there when him and Pete Clarke played the other flute. They used two flutes.

I would like to ask you just right now, just to interject this. What do you attribute to that the young black musicians don't have -- we have this era of all these instrumentalists like Bennie Carter and Chick Webb and Don Redmon and Garvin Bushell and Sam Wooding that played all of these great, all these instruments, these academic instruments like the flute and piccolo and bassoon -- and in this era we don't have too much of that.

I attribute that to disc jockeys, to our booking agents, to the trend of music that they are putting in front of these people. There's not music, actually, that you can learn anything from. There's no more big bands where that you can learn to play with a section. Everything is so individualistic now, you see. And everybody, if you listen, they all sound the same. They sound the same. You can make a million dollars on one record and a guitar player can learn five chords and get rich.
